title: Output of the iteration-plan agent: a diagnosis and a proposed correction

dureeCoherente.description: Does the real file duration match the wanted duration (gap of half a second at most)? If false, no writing diagnosis: `changements` stays empty. Always true without a thumbnail sheet (no real duration was measured).

symptome.description: (French) What is wrong, with the thumbnail instants (« à 4 s, l'épée apparaît »). Without a thumbnail sheet: the user's request restated in one sentence, no instants.

cause.description: (French) The precise cause targeted by this correction, only one. Points to a lexicon entry when one exists.

categorie.description: `decoupage-scenario` = the cause is not in the prompt (to be handled separately): `changements` stays empty. `modele` = the same symptom survived three corrections aimed at different causes (goes with `abandon.propose`). `autre` = a cause that fits no other category.

changements.description: The smallest text change that treats the cause: replacements of passages in the FINAL prompt (labels <Subject N>/<Picture N>/<Audio N> kept as they are, <d> tags intact). Empty if the cause is not in the prompt, if the duration is inconsistent, or on abandon.

avant.description: Exact passage replaced, copied as is from promptActuel (a single occurrence in the section).

apres.description: (English) Replacing passage, with the same labels and the same <d> tags.

verification.description: (French) What to look at on the next render to know whether the correction worked.

entreeLexique.description: (English) Optional. Lexicon candidate, to be entered only after a render that solved the symptom (never written by the application).

reecriture.description: Required. false for a retouch of passages (default). true when the instruction changes WHAT HAPPENS in the plan (a different action, place, ending, an attempt, an element added or removed, a new shot sequence): it is no longer a retouch of passages but a rewrite of the plan. Then `changements` stays empty and the NEXT field, `nouvelleDescription`, is the plan rewritten, complete; the application rewrites the whole sheet from it.

dureeSecondes.description: Optional. The plan's NEW generation duration, whole seconds from 5 to 15, ONLY when the user's instruction asks for another duration (« passe-le à 12 secondes », « allonge-le »). Omit it otherwise: the plan keeps its duration. When you give it, re-time the shots' `At MM:SS.mmm` markers in `changements` so they spread over the new duration (or, on a rewrite, the whole sheet is rewritten for it).

nouvelleDescription.description: (French) The plan's NEW description (its intention), complete, ending with « État en fin de plan : … » (where the characters who matter stand and what they face, relative to fixed landmarks of the place, never to the camera; the state of what changed). REQUIRED when `reecriture` is true: write it right here, it is the whole point of a rewrite (an answer with `reecriture` true and an empty description is refused). Also give it when a retouch changes the state it leaves to the next plan. Empty string when the description stays as it is.

assetsManquants.description: Optional. Assets you SUGGEST to create because the cause is a missing image and NO registry asset fits (search the registry first). You create nothing and cite none in your passages: the user creates it, generates its image, then iterates again. A STATE of a subject (character, creature, set, prop) has the same type as the subject and its `parent`.

code.description: Proposed code, type prefix + short lowercase name (CHAR_, DEC_, PROP_, VFX_).

parent.description: Code of the base subject (registry) when the asset is a state of it.

description.description: (French) What is seen, as in the registry.

abandon.description: propose = true only if three corrections targeting different causes failed (see historique); otherwise propose = false and empty raison.

raison.description: (French) What was tried, and the proposed replacement move.

references.description: Optional. When the cause is a missing or excessive reference image (a registry asset that should have been cited, or that disturbs the render): the references to add (by registry CODE) and to remove. The code assigns the labels, renumbers the remaining images and updates subject_definitions and retention_analysis: you touch neither the numbers nor those two sections for this. An added reference is cited in your passages as `[[CODE]]`.

asset.description: Code of a registry asset (never invented), not yet a reference of this plan.

nom.description: (English) Its name, as it will be written in subject_definitions.

role.description: (French) Optional. Its role in this plan.

retirer.description: Codes of the plan's current image references to remove.
